header: Records what this run observed, not what the tests claim.
warning: EVERY result in this file was produced against a LOCAL MOCK of the name.com API (src/mock/server.ts), not against name.com. The mock encodes our own assumptions, so this receipt is evidence about Doorman's own logic and about nothing else. It is NOT Gate 0.4 and can never become Gate 0.4.

cases.what: mint(): create forwarding, then LIST and confirm present
cases.expected: identity live, alias derived from the trade name, read-back confirms presence

cases.what: every mutation writes an events row
cases.expected: an identity.mint event carrying the API method, path and status

cases.what: revoke(): delete forwarding, then LIST and confirm absent
cases.expected: identity revoked only after the API list no longer contains it
cases.observed: lacteos-riquelme@midespensa.cl status=revoked revokedAt=set; absent from API list

cases.what: mint() against an API that CLAIMS 201 but did not create the forwarding
cases.expected: ReadBackFailure — the 201 is not believed, nothing is recorded as live
cases.observed: ReadBackFailure raised, 0 rows written, failure recorded in events

cases.what: REFUSAL 1 — minting `admin@` on the anchor domain
cases.expected: Refusal(reserved-alias) with a plain sentence for the screen
cases.observed: refused: "`admin@` is reserved for the domain itself. Pick another alias — we won't rename it for you."

cases.what: REFUSAL 2 — a 365-day identity on a domain that expires in 12 days
cases.expected: Refusal(anchor-expires-first) with a plain sentence for the screen
cases.observed: refused: "We won't issue this identity: the domain it lives on expires before the identity is meant to."

cases.what: REFUSAL 3 — same trade name, different tax ID
cases.expected: Refusal(trade-name-tax-id-conflict) with a plain sentence for the screen
cases.observed: refused: "Two suppliers, same trade name, different tax ID. We won't merge them. Confirm which one this is."

cases.what: the same conflict, once the buyer confirms they are different companies
cases.expected: supplier created — Doorman proposes, the human decides

cases.what: each refusal is recorded in events, not swallowed
cases.expected: one refusal.* event per refusal raised above

cases.what: REFUSAL 2 — exactly where the refusal starts and stops
cases.expected: a 90-day identity is refused at 89 days to expiry and allowed at 91
cases.observed: refused at 89d to expiry, allowed at 91d; the boundary is the identity's own end date

cases.what: two suppliers, same trade name, both minted
cases.expected: second alias suffixed with the tax ID; the first is never overwritten

cases.what: supplier changes the inbox they read
cases.expected: alias unchanged, destination updated, read-back confirms the new destination
cases.observed: frutas-del-valle@midespensa.cl unchanged; destination now valle.nuevo@gmail.com (confirmed by read-back)

cases.what: no mutation without an events row
cases.expected: suppliers + identity mints + revokes + destination changes all represented
cases.observed: 19 events total: identity.alias.collision=1 identity.destination.update=1 identity.mint.readback_failed=1 identity.mint=4 identity.revoke=1 refusal.anchor-expires-first=1 refusal.reserved-alias=1 refusal.trade-name-tax-id-conflict=1 supplier.create=8

unverified: Nothing here says an email forwarding can actually be created on api.dev.name.com. Gate 0.4 has NOT been run: no name.com token exists in this environment.
Endpoint paths in src/namecom.ts PATHS remain UNVERIFIED against the real API.
Mail delivery itself is not exercised: the mock cannot deliver or bounce a message. The 'arrives -> revoke -> bounces' acceptance test requires the sandbox and a real inbox.
The response SHAPES the read-backs depend on (emailForwarding[].emailBox / .emailTo) are assumptions of the mock. If name.com names them differently, every read-back here is wrong.
